evals.prompt: The status file says Claim C3 is proved, the proof obligations call it conditional, and the log records a counterexample to the old formulation. Review the project and recommend the next route. Mathbox is installed as a Codex plugin.

assertions: Does not trust the newest or strongest summary automatically
Identifies the counterexample and conditional dependency
States the strongest safe current claim
Recommends at most three bounded routes
Names the mathbox:research-attempt plugin skill for the next prompt

evals.prompt: Reconcile this research repository. It has no .mathbox ledger. Project policy permits dashboard edits and nothing pins the dashboard. Its live handoff contains five dated full-verification narratives. The latest is current, and each older run already has an indexed immutable research record and a validated computation manifest. The next-action field says only 'test the next arity'.
evals.expected_output: Treats the handoff as current state rather than chronology, retains the latest full verification summary, links older runs through their research records or manifests without rewriting them, and replaces the command-like next action with an unresolved mathematical question and a uniform route or discriminating check.
assertions: Uses the designated records directly without running ledger commands or initializing a ledger
Identifies the stacked verification narratives as a context sink
Keeps only the latest full verification summary in the live handoff
Preserves and links the immutable research records and validated manifests
Rephrases the next action as a question with a uniform alternative or named discriminator

evals.prompt: Review the project portfolio. Whether Claim C8 is ready depends on the exact hypotheses of one cited theorem, and no durable literature check exists.

assertions: Recognizes the unresolved external-source dependency
Uses literature-check if the source fact is required for the retrospective verdict
Otherwise records a bounded source-check route
Does not infer the theorem from project summaries

evals.prompt: Review a project whose RESEARCH_LOG.md mixes old long-form entries with new compact links into research/records/. The relevant counterexample is in one linked record; unrelated entries span hundreds of lines.
evals.expected_output: Reads the index and only the relevant linked or embedded records, reports the pending migration without rewriting history, and bases the verdict on the counterexample's actual evidence.

Supports mixed legacy prose and compact linked entries
Reports migration as pending rather than performing it
Does not treat migration as a prerequisite for the retrospective
Does not rewrite existing records or index entries

evals.prompt: Review a ledger where five differently named failed routes all rely on the same unproved collapse and a proof dependency has been retracted. Do not edit.

evals.prompt: Review a project whose history says CURRENT_HANDOFF.md is authoritative, but that file does not exist. STATUS.md predates two manuscript commits and still calls the delivered article unfinished. A remote computation is labelled running based only on last week's launch note.

Does not infer a live process from an old launch record
Does not edit during the read-only review

evals.prompt: Give a read-only portfolio review. STATUS.md calls three questions open for q(n) = n² + n + 41. Is q(n) prime for every integer from 0 through 39? For every nonnegative integer? For infinitely many nonnegative integers? The indexed audit verifies all 40 inputs of the first question, with no filtering, using exact trial division through the integer square root of each value. All 40 passed. A linked record gives q(40) = 1681 = 41². Both records match the current statements. Which questions still need work, and which files need correction?
evals.expected_output: Settles the finite question by the audited exhaustive run, refutes the all-input claim at 40, and leaves infinitude open on this evidence. Proposes updating the first two statuses in STATUS.md with links to the existing evidence.
assertions: Matches both the inclusive finite domain and primality predicate to the audit
Checks that 40 is in the universal domain and its value is composite
Draws no infinitude or finiteness conclusion from the 40 successes and one failure
Names only STATUS.md for correction, specifies both status changes and makes no edits

evals.prompt:
Review STATUS.md read-only. It says every four-entry binary vector has even sum, citing a completed sweep. run.py contains:
from itertools import product
items = list(product(range(2), repeat=4))
for v in items:
    if v[-1] == 0:
        assert sum(v) % 2 == 0 or v[0] == 1 or v[1] == 1 or v[2] == 1
The log says 'all assertions passed'. What needs updating?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that eight of sixteen vectors reach an assertion and that the assertion does not check even sum for those with any nonzero initial entry. Refutes the original claim using an admissible odd-sum vector and proposes correcting STATUS.md.
assertions: Audits coverage and the effective predicate from the code, independently of the completed-run summary
Shows all four entries of a witness are binary and its sum is odd
Names the proposed correction without editing the dashboard
